title: Enterprise LLM Search
seoTitle: Design an LLM-Powered Enterprise Search System
description: Design an LLM-powered enterprise search system — connectors to company tools, chunking and embedding documents, hybrid retrieval, permission-aware results, grounded answers with citations, and evaluation.
author: Editorial Team

blocks.title: What is Enterprise LLM Search?
blocks.text: Enterprise LLM search (Glean, or "ask our docs" assistants) lets employees ask questions in plain language — "What's our parental leave policy in Germany?" — and get a direct answer drawn from the company's own documents, wikis, tickets and chats, with links to the sources. It combines a search engine over many internal tools with a large language model that writes the answer (**retrieval-augmented generation**, or RAG), and it must never show someone a document they aren't allowed to see.

items: The system should index content from company tools (docs, wikis, email, tickets, chat) through connectors.
Users should be able to search with keywords or natural-language questions.
The system should return a generated answer with **citations** to the source documents, plus a ranked result list.
Results and answers must respect each user's permissions in the source systems.
Users can give feedback (thumbs up/down) on answers.
Agents that take actions in tools.
Training or fine-tuning our own LLM.

blocks.question: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?

items: Never leak content across permissions — the most important requirement.
Fresh: edits and new documents searchable within minutes; permission changes applied within minutes.
Answer latency: first tokens in < 2 s, results list in < 500 ms.
Grounded: answers come from retrieved sources, with citations, and say "I don't know" otherwise.
Scale to large companies: ~100M documents per tenant, thousands of queries per minute, strict tenant isolation.
Perfect answer quality on every query.
**Source connector**: integration with a tool, credentials, sync cursor.
**Document**: tenant, source, URL, title, content, author, updated at, **ACL** (users and groups allowed).
**Chunk**: a passage of a document (~300-800 tokens) with its embedding and inherited ACL.
**Identity mapping**: a user's identities and group memberships across tools.
**Query log**: query, retrieved chunks, answer, feedback.

blocks.text: **Connectors** for each tool sync documents incrementally (webhooks where available, polling with cursors otherwise), including each document's **permissions**. An ingestion pipeline extracts text, splits it into **chunks**, computes **embeddings**, and writes to two indexes: a keyword index (BM25) and a **vector index**, both storing the ACL on every chunk.

A query is run against **both** indexes (hybrid retrieval): keyword search catches exact names and codes, vector search catches paraphrases. Both are filtered by the user's permissions, results are merged, and a **re-ranker** model reorders the top ~50 candidates by relevance, freshness and authority.

The top chunks are placed in a prompt with instructions to answer **only from the provided sources** and cite them. The LLM's answer is streamed to the user with citation markers linking to the source documents. If retrieval found nothing relevant, the assistant says it couldn't find an answer.

Queries, retrieved chunks, answers and feedback are logged. An **evaluation set** of real questions with known answers is re-run when prompts, models or ranking change, measuring retrieval recall, answer correctness and citation accuracy.

approach.text: Retrieve from all documents, generate an answer, then hide citations the user can't open.

challenges.text: The answer text itself may already contain confidential information from documents the user can't see.

approach.text: Retrieve candidates, then drop chunks the user can't access before building the prompt.

challenges.text: If most top results are restricted, few relevant chunks remain, and relevance suffers.

blocks.title: ACL filtering inside retrieval + fresh permission sync

approach.text: Store each chunk's **allowed principals** (users and groups) in both indexes and pass the user's **expanded group memberships** as a filter **during retrieval**, so only permitted chunks are ever candidates. Sync permission changes from sources quickly (and treat "unknown permissions" as private). For highly sensitive sources, **re-check access** against the source API at query time before showing results.

challenges.text: Group expansion for large organisations can be big; cache it per user and refresh on change events.

blocks.text: 2) How do we keep answers grounded and useful?

Retrieval quality drives answer quality. Good chunking keeps headings with their text; hybrid retrieval plus a re-ranker raises recall; including document titles, dates and authors in the prompt helps the model prefer recent, authoritative sources. Prompts require citations for every claim, and a lightweight check verifies that cited chunks actually support the answer. When sources conflict (an old policy page versus a new one), the answer says so and cites both.

Mention cost and latency: answer generation is the most expensive step. Cache answers for identical questions per permission set, use a smaller model for simple queries, and stream tokens to make latency feel shorter.
3) How do we isolate tenants and scale indexing?

Each customer's data lives in **separate indexes** (or strictly partitioned ones) with tenant-specific encryption keys, and queries can never cross tenants. Ingestion is a queue-based pipeline that scales workers per tenant; initial syncs of millions of documents are throttled to respect source API rate limits, while incremental updates take priority so fresh edits appear quickly. Embeddings are recomputed only for changed chunks.

quiz.question: Why combine keyword and vector search?
options: Keywords catch exact terms; vectors catch paraphrases — together they improve recall
quiz.explanation: Hybrid retrieval covers both exact and semantic matches.

quiz.question: Where should permission filtering happen?
options: Inside retrieval, using ACLs stored on every chunk
quiz.explanation: Restricted content must never reach the prompt.

quiz.question: What makes an answer grounded?
options: It's written only from retrieved sources and cites them
quiz.explanation: Citations let users verify; no sources means 'I don't know'.

quiz.question: How do we check that changes to prompts or models don't make things worse?
options: Re-run an evaluation set of real questions with known answers
quiz.explanation: Offline evaluation catches regressions before rollout.
